activity_kiss_of_the_sea.lede:
Kiss of the Sea is an outdoor multimedia show at Sunset Town combining a water stage, projection, lighting, lasers, fire, music and fireworks. The stage and grandstand are described as accommodating around 5,000 spectators; the main performance usually lasts about 30 minutes and may be followed by fireworks.
This is a show that needs to be planned in advance. Do not buy a ticket simply because the fireworks look impressive in photographs: seat location, viewing angle, weather and the inclusions of each ticket category make a significant difference to the real experience.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A large water stage, tiered grandstand and layered multimedia production
infographic.note:
Kiss of the Sea is more than a conventional stage show. The experience includes:
• An outdoor water stage.
• Water screens and projection systems.
• Lighting, lasers, fire and stage effects.
• Live performers.
• A tiered grandstand with multiple ticket sections.
• Fireworks after the main performance when scheduled.
The large capacity allows many visitors to attend, but it also means reaching the correct gate, checking tickets, finding your seat and leaving after the show all take time. Groups should agree on a meeting point before entering.

infographic.label: BEFORE YOU BUY
infographic.value: Check the ticket category and seating plan
infographic.note:
Ticket categories can differ in:
• Grandstand position.
• Viewing angle towards the stage and water.
• Distance from the water screen.
• Combination-package benefits.
• Date-change or refund conditions.
• Whether Kiss Bridge, the cable car or another service is included.
Do not compare tickets by the lowest price alone. Look at the seating map and confirm whether you are buying show admission, a combination ticket or a package with additional benefits.

infographic.label: BUILD THE EVENING AROUND IT
infographic.value: Work backwards from show time
infographic.note:
For a large show with a fixed start, the whole evening is easier if the performance time becomes the anchor. Fit Kiss Bridge, dinner, photographs and other activities around it.
Leave time for:
• Walking to the grandstand.
• Queueing at the entrance.
• Finding your seat.
• Buying water or using the restroom.
• Heavy pedestrian traffic after the show.
Avoid scheduling another distant stop immediately afterwards, especially with young children or older adults.

sections.heading: This is a show to schedule, not something to fit in by chance
sections.body:
A large seated show with a fixed start does not work well as “we'll see it if we have time”. Arrive late and you may miss the opening, lose the chance to settle comfortably or spend time waiting outside.
A relaxed evening could look like this:
• Late afternoon: arrive at Sunset Town and walk around.
• Before the show: have a light meal or early dinner.
• Before start time: enter the grandstand.
• After the show: watch the fireworks if scheduled, then leave by the route you already identified.

sections.heading: Firework photographs do not tell the whole story
sections.body:
The fireworks are only the finale. The main experience also comes from the water stage, projection, music and the interaction between performers and technology.
Your seat affects how these layers come together. A distant section may offer a strong overall view but less detail; a very close section can feel immersive but may not always be the easiest position for seeing the whole stage at once.

visitor_questions: Has today's show changed because of the weather?
Where is this ticket category on the seating plan?
Does the ticket include the fireworks and any other benefits?
How early should I arrive before the show starts?
Where is the most practical pick-up point afterwards?
Which grandstand area is easiest to enter and leave with young children?

sources.label: Sunset Town / Sun World - Check current schedule and tickets

place_cua_can.lede:
Cua Can is where river, estuary and beach meet, creating a landscape that feels different from a straightforward seaside stop. Its character comes from the transition between freshwater, brackish water and the sea, together with riverside communities and activities such as boating or kayaking when conditions are suitable.

The Cua Can River is commonly described as being about 15 km long and flowing out to sea in the Cua Can area. That does not mean the entire river is a visitor route. Distinguish between a riverside viewpoint, Cua Can Beach and the specific kayak route offered by an operator.

infographic.label: WHAT IS IT?
infographic.value: A riverside community, estuary and beach area
infographic.note:
Cua Can is more than a beach. The area includes:

• The river mouth where the water reaches the sea.
• River sections and banks that can be observed or explored through organised activities.
• Residential areas and fishing communities along the water.
• The beach, where conditions change noticeably with wind, waves, rain and tide.

Because the experience is spread out, know where you are going and what you want to do. Looking at the estuary is different from kayaking upriver; swimming at the beach is different again from joining a guided route.

infographic.label: EXPERIENCE
infographic.value: Kayaking, slow boat rides and observing the riverbanks
infographic.note:
Kayaking offers a slower way to read the landscape, letting you control your pace and look closely at vegetation, calmer water and daily life along the banks. Depending on the starting point and actual conditions, some routes may also include mangrove areas, fishing communities or stretches near the estuary.

A boat with a driver suits groups that want less physical effort, or those travelling with young children or older adults. Kayaking is better for people who can balance independently, follow safety instructions and respond when the kayak changes direction.

Cua Can does not need to become an endurance adventure. Its value is in moving slowly and understanding the river environment. First-time paddlers should choose a short route on calm water with guidance.

infographic.label: GOOD TO KNOW
infographic.value: Water level, rain and wind can change the whole experience
infographic.note:
An estuary is a constantly changing environment. Water level, current, tide, rain and wind can affect whether a trip can start, how safe it is and how far you can paddle.

Before getting on the water, confirm:

• Whether today's route stays on the river, reaches the estuary or approaches the sea.
• Whether the water level and current suit beginners.
• Whether life jackets are compulsory and provided in the correct sizes.
• Whether a guide or rescue option is available if someone becomes tired.
• Whether heavy rain, thunderstorms or strong winds are expected.

Do not paddle out towards the open estuary or leave the group if you lack experience. A life jacket, clear safety instructions and staying on the agreed route matter more than getting a perfect photograph.

sections.heading: A side of Phu Quoc that is not only about the sea
sections.body:
Cua Can reveals another part of the island's geography: a place where the sea connects with a river, an estuary, vegetated banks and local communities. It can be a welcome change of pace after days spent at beaches, theme parks or resorts.

The scenery is not “ready-made” every day. The water can be murky; wind, rain or a stronger current can change the experience. That does not make Cua Can less worthwhile. It simply means this is a natural environment that needs to be visited at the right time and in the right conditions.

sections.heading: Go to observe, not to turn it into a race
sections.body:
There is no need to compete over who paddles furthest. If you are new to kayaking, go with someone experienced, wear a life jacket, stay with the group and choose an appropriate stretch of river.

Families are better served by shorter routes with rest points and a sensible duration. More experienced paddlers can choose a longer route, but should still follow local guidance and account for weather, tide and current.

visitor_questions: Which section of the river does today's route cover?
Are the current and water level safe for a first-time paddler?
Does the route approach the estuary or remain on sheltered river water?
Are life jackets and other safety equipment provided in suitable sizes?
If someone becomes tired halfway through, is there a support or return-to-shore option?

sources.label: VisitPhuQuoc - Four-day Phu Quoc itinerary including Cua Can kayaking

place_night_market.lede:
Duong Dong Night Market, also known as Phu Quoc Night Market, is currently operating around Bach Dang Street and remains one of the easiest places to experience the evening rhythm of food and shopping in central Phu Quoc.
It is important to distinguish today's Phu Quoc Night Market from older market sites. A Visit Phu Quoc update published on 29 September 2026 still describes more than 100 stalls and daily opening around 15:00-23:00, while the destination page on the same tourism portal lists roughly 18:00-23:30. Individual stalls can keep different hours, so treat these as approximate operating windows rather than one fixed closing time.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A central street of food stalls and shopping
infographic.note:
The market has generally been described as a street-based experience with several types of vendor:
• Seafood and dishes cooked to order.
• Snacks, grilled food and local specialities.
• Fish sauce, pepper, sim wine and packaged products.
• Souvenirs, handicrafts and tourism goods.
• Drinks, desserts and takeaway gifts.
This is not a traditional market laid out in large permanent commodity sections. The experience centres on walking, looking at stalls, choosing food and shopping along a relatively busy street.
A basic visit often takes around 60-90 minutes. If you eat dinner there, wait for food to be cooked or travel with a large group, allow longer. Evenings have traditionally been the busiest period, but opening hours and the current level of activity need to be confirmed for the day.

infographic.label: EATING SEAFOOD
infographic.value: Ask the price, unit and cooking charge before ordering
infographic.note:
Food may be priced by:
• Portion.
• Plate.
• Kilogram.
• Size of the individual seafood item.
• Type of ingredient.
• A separate cooking fee.
Before ordering, ask whether the quoted price includes cooking, vegetables, dipping sauces, seasonings and side dishes. If you choose seafood from the display, confirm both the weight and the price for the exact item selected.
Do not assume every stall uses the same pricing or hygiene standards. A busy stall is not enough by itself; also look at how ingredients are stored and where food is prepared.

infographic.label: HOW TO FIT IT IN
infographic.value: Eat a little, then keep walking
infographic.note:
The market can be combined with Dinh Cau, the Duong Dong river mouth and central streets. It does not need to take up the entire evening.
A light itinerary might be:
• Walk around Dinh Cau or the riverfront.
• Try a few dishes at the market.
• Buy packaged local products.
• Continue through the town centre before heading back.
With young children or older adults, avoid the most crowded periods where possible, agree on a meeting point and do not let the group spread too far apart.

sections.heading: The night market is one slice of Duong Dong after dark
sections.body:
Local tourism sources describe the present market as developing from the former Dinh Cau Night Market and old Bach Dang Night Market, with food, seafood, local products and souvenir stalls.
An update dated 29 September 2026 still describes more than 100 stalls operating daily. References to an older market site closing should therefore not be read as meaning that today's Phu Quoc Night Market has closed. Official sources give slightly different opening hours, so if your plan depends on arriving late, check the same-day situation.

sections.heading: International visitors should ask about ingredients before trying unfamiliar food
sections.body:
Dipping sauces, satay, marinades and toppings may contain fish, shrimp, shellfish, peanuts or soy. Anyone with an allergy should ask each stall directly because recipes and cooking utensils differ.
Vegetarian travellers, people who avoid fish sauce or those who do not eat seafood should also be explicit before ordering. Asking only “does this contain meat?” may not be enough because broth, dipping sauce or seasoning can still contain animal ingredients.

visitor_questions: Is the market operating today?
Is this dish priced by portion or by weight?
Does the price already include cooking?
What type and weight of seafood am I being charged for?
Does the sauce or dipping sauce contain peanuts, shrimp or fish?
Is there a seated eating area that works well with young children?

sources.label: VisitPhuQuoc - Phu Quoc Night Market
VisitPhuQuoc - Phu Quoc Night Market, 17 April 2026

place_bai_truong.lede:
Bai Truong is not a small beach with a single entrance. The name refers to a long stretch of Phu Quoc's west coast, made up of different beach sections, residential areas, resorts, restaurants, seaside parks and sunset viewpoints.
Travel sources often describe Bai Truong as being nearly 20 km long, extending south from the Dinh Cau area towards An Thoi. The exact figure depends on where the start and end points are defined, so “a coastline of nearly 20 km” is more useful than treating it as an absolute measurement.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A long west-coast strip divided into very different beach sections
infographic.note:
Bai Truong can be understood as several different areas:
• Sections close to central Duong Dong.
• Areas near the airport and Duong To.
• Resort, hotel and restaurant clusters.
• Sections with public beach access.
• Places suited to sunset, swimming or walking.
• Shoreline affected differently by development, tide and seasonal winds.
Because the coastline is so long, two places both called Bai Truong can feel very different in sand, water, visitor density, access, services and privacy.
Do not use “Bai Truong” as a single map pin. Identify the actual beach section, business name or access point you intend to use.

infographic.label: WHY GO?
infographic.value: Sunset, resort time and easy access
infographic.note:
The west coast is well placed for sunset and works naturally with beach time, food and accommodation. Bai Truong is also close to the airport, Duong Dong, Duong To and many resorts, making it practical for shorter itineraries.
Common reasons to go include:
• Watching sunset.
• Swimming when conditions are suitable.
• Walking or using resort and restaurant services.
• Coastal photography.
• Combining the beach with central areas and nearby accommodation.
If your only goal is sunset, you do not need to find the most distant section of beach. A place with easy access, parking and a clear horizon is often the more practical choice.

infographic.label: YOU NEED TO CHOOSE
infographic.value: Choose the correct beach section and access point
infographic.note:
Before going, ask:
• Which part of Bai Truong you actually intend to visit.
• Whether there is public access or the route passes through a hotel or resort.
• Where vehicles can park.
• Whether the area is suitable for swimming or mainly for views.
• Whether toilets, showers, loungers or lifeguards are available.
• Which nearby position gives the best sunset view that day.
Do not assume every part of Bai Truong has the same access rights or facilities.

sections.heading: One beach name, but in practice an entire coastline
sections.body:
Local travel sources describe Bai Truong as extending for nearly 20 km along Phu Quoc's southwest coast. At that scale, it cannot be experienced as one single beach.
A family staying near Duong To may simply need the closest practical access point. A couple looking for sunset may prefer a section with a restaurant. Walkers should choose a clear start and end point rather than imagine they can cover the whole coastline in one outing.

sections.heading: Sunset is the strength, but the beach still depends on the day's weather
sections.body:
The west coast naturally faces sunset, but sky colour, cloud, waves, seaweed and beach condition change with season and weather.
A beautiful photograph from one day does not represent the whole coastline. Heavy cloud may reduce the colour but create softer light; strong wind may make the sea dramatic to look at while making it unsuitable for swimming.

visitor_questions: Does this section have public access, or is it connected to an accommodation property?
Which area is best for swimming and sunset today?
Is there parking and a toilet nearby?
Are there lifeguards or sea-condition warnings in this area?
How early should I arrive before sunset to find a convenient place?

sources.label: VisitPhuQuoc - Bai Truong, Phu Quoc, 17 September 2026
VisitPhuQuoc - Bai Truong, 9 November 2025

place_exotica.lede:
Exotica Village is the adventure and thrill-ride zone on Hon Thom within Sun World Hon Thom. It is a different experience from Aquatopia: one focuses on water attractions, while the other is built more around height, speed, movement and adrenaline.
Do not choose rides from their names alone. Check height limits, health restrictions, waiting times and how Exotica fits with the cable car, Aquatopia and beach time on the same day.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: An adventure zone within a full Hon Thom day
infographic.note:
Exotica Village can be thought of through several types of experience:
• Elevated attractions.
• Motion-based and thrill rides.
• Observation or panoramic-view experiences.
• Queueing and rest areas.
• Connections to Aquatopia, the beach and the cable-car station.
Eagle Eye is promoted as a 120-metre observation tower, with a cabin lifting visitors to about 80 metres; published capacity is around 70 people per ride.
Those figures help explain why Exotica is not somewhere to simply walk through in a few minutes if you want to ride several attractions. The real time required depends on queues, operating status and which rides suit each person in your group.

infographic.label: HIGHLIGHTS
infographic.value: Wooden coaster, Eagle Eye and attractions that can change over time
infographic.note:
Moc Xa Thinh No is commonly promoted as the zone's signature thrill ride. Eagle Eye is more about panoramic views from height than pure speed. Other attractions can be added, changed or operated differently over time.
Distinguish between:
• Speed and acceleration rides.
• Height-based experiences.
• Scenic rides.
• Attractions with strict health or height requirements.
Someone who enjoys a high viewpoint may not enjoy a fast drop or spinning ride. Families should choose according to each person's tolerance rather than push everyone into the same category.

infographic.label: BEFORE YOU QUEUE
infographic.value: Check height, health conditions and the current wait
infographic.note:
Before joining a queue, check:
• Minimum or maximum height.
• Restrictions relating to heart conditions, blood pressure, neck or back problems and pregnancy.
• Whether glasses, phones or small bags are allowed.
• Current waiting time.
• Whether the ride is operating normally.
• Whether there is a practical waiting area for anyone not riding.
Thrill rides can leave people tired, dizzy or uncomfortable afterwards. Do not stack too many in a row simply to get maximum value from the ticket.

sections.heading: Do not treat Aquatopia and Exotica as the same experience
sections.body:
Sun World presents Exotica as the adventure and thrill zone, while Aquatopia is the water park. They use your energy, clothing and queueing time in very different ways.
If your group covers several age ranges, decide which area is the main priority before you arrive. Anyone who does not want intense rides can spend time at the beach, viewpoints or rest areas instead of waiting beside every queue.

sections.heading: A good Hon Thom day does not require doing everything
sections.body:
The cable car, water park, adventure rides and beach all compete for the same limited time. Choosing a few important experiences is usually more enjoyable than rushing from ride to ride.
Possible combinations include:
• Exotica + viewpoints + beach rest.
• Aquatopia + one suitable Exotica ride.
• Cable car + Eagle Eye + photography.
• One main zone, with the rest of the time for food and relaxation.

visitor_questions: What height or health restrictions apply to this ride?
Are Moc Xa Thinh No and Eagle Eye operating today?
What is the current waiting time?
Is there an attraction suitable for someone who does not want a thrill ride?
What time is the last cable car back to An Thoi?

sources.label: VisitPhuQuoc - Sun World Hon Thom and Exotica Village
VisitPhuQuoc - Sun World Hon Thom

place_suoi_tranh.lede:
Suoi Tranh is a nature stop close to the central part of the island, but the experience depends heavily on the water season. The same stream can look completely different in the wet season and during a dry spell.
The stream is described as originating in the Ham Ninh mountains and running for about 15 km. Visitors, however, normally access only a short section within the tourism area, not the full length of the stream. Some sources describe a walking route of roughly 1.5 km and around 30 minutes to the waterfall area, but the route actually open should be checked on the day.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A long natural stream, with only one section developed for visitors
infographic.note:
There are two different scales to keep in mind at Suoi Tranh:
• Natural scale: the stream and its network of channels extending from the Ham Ninh mountain area.
• Visitor scale: the trail, bridges, stone steps, rest areas and waterfall section that can actually be reached.
You do not need a full day to “cover” the stream. A basic visit usually involves:
• Walking from the entrance or parking area into the forest route.
• Following the trail.
• Stopping at water, rock and waterfall areas.
• Resting or swimming if conditions allow.
• Returning along the route.
A visit often takes around half a day, but the timing changes with walking pace, water season, trail conditions and whether you stop to swim.

infographic.label: THE DECIDING FACTOR
infographic.value: Whether there is enough water
infographic.note:
The wet season usually gives the stream more flow, greener vegetation and stronger-looking falls. Some sources suggest roughly May-September or June-November as wetter periods, but a fixed monthly window should not be applied to every year.
What matters on the actual day is:
• Whether recent rain has produced enough flow.
• Whether rain has been so heavy that the water is muddy or the route unsafe.
• Whether pools and waterfall sections are open to visitors.
• Whether swimming areas are safe and managed.
A photograph of a full waterfall shows one moment in time, not what visitors should expect every month.

infographic.label: WHAT TO BRING
infographic.value: Shoes with grip, light gear and a plan for wet ground
infographic.note:
Forest paths, stone steps and rocks beside the stream can be slippery. Bring:
• Shoes with good grip.
• Light, quick-drying clothing.
• A waterproof pouch for your phone.
• Drinking water.
• Insect repellent if needed.
• A change of clothes if you plan to enter the water.
Avoid smooth-soled footwear, climbing onto high rocks or standing directly below a waterfall when the flow is strong.

sections.heading: Check the season before you judge it from photographs
sections.body:
Suoi Tranh is close to the centre and often appears in half-day itineraries. Promotional photographs, however, are usually taken when the vegetation is lush, the water is full and the light is favourable.
Open Phu Quoc does not use a full-flow waterfall image as a promise that the site always looks that way. Before going, decide whether your purpose is a forest walk, scenery, a picnic or swimming, because each needs different conditions.

sections.heading: After rain can be prettier - and more slippery
sections.body:
More water can make the landscape more attractive, but it also makes rocks and access paths more slippery. Prolonged heavy rain can turn the water muddy, increase the flow or lead to restricted areas.
The ideal condition is not “the more rain, the better”. It is often after moderate rainfall, once the weather has cleared, with enough water remaining and the route still reasonably safe.

visitor_questions: Is there much water in the stream today?
Is the trail slippery after rain, or are any areas currently restricted?
Roughly how long does it take to walk from the entrance to the waterfall area?
Which areas are open for swimming?
Has there been any recent warning about rising water or heavy rain?
Is today's route suitable for young children or older adults?

sources.label: VisitPhuQuoc - Suoi Tranh
VisitPhuQuoc - Suoi Tranh, 10 September 2026

place_other_streams.lede:
Suoi Da Ban, Da Ngon and Suoi Tien should not be treated as three interchangeable versions of Suoi Tranh. Each differs in landscape, terrain, access, walking distance and how much water it carries through the seasons.
These are places that should not be scheduled from attractive photographs alone. A stream can look spectacular when water levels are high but also become more slippery, difficult and risky. In a drier period, access may be easier while the waterfalls and natural pools are less impressive.

infographic.label: DA BAN
infographic.value: Broad rock slabs, easy to recognise and well suited to a picnic
infographic.note:
Suoi Da Ban is in the Cua Duong area, about 10 km from central Duong Dong. Its name is associated with the large, relatively flat rock slabs that lie along the stream.
The experience can include:
• Access from residential roads towards the stream.
• Large rock slabs beside the water.
• Places to sit, eat or picnic.
• Deeper and shallower water that changes with the season.
Da Ban is often easier to imagine for families or groups of friends wanting a light outdoor stop. But “flat rock” does not mean “non-slip”. Moss, flowing water and rain can change the surface very quickly.

infographic.label: SUOI TIEN
infographic.value: More forested, picnic-oriented and removed from the built-up island
infographic.note:
Suoi Tien is commonly associated with the Ham Ninh area and a more natural forest setting. It is not the sort of attraction for visitors who want to step off a vehicle, walk a few metres and take a photograph.
The experience may involve:
• Walking on forest or dirt paths.
• Following the stream across rocks and vegetation.
• Finding a place to rest or picnic.
• Swimming if water level and safety conditions allow.
A more natural setting also means services, signs, phone signal and immediate assistance may be more limited than at a heavily developed attraction. Go with someone who knows the route or an operator with local experience.

infographic.label: DA NGON
infographic.value: Multiple waterfall sections, more difficult and requiring greater caution
infographic.note:
Suoi Da Ngon is often described as having a more complex natural landscape with several waterfall levels. Some sources refer to a system of around seven falls, but route length and ease of access can differ by season and starting point.
This is not suitable for every visitor. Slippery ground, large rocks, climbing sections and stronger water can be difficult for anyone unfamiliar with the terrain.
Do not put Da Ngon into a family itinerary simply because the photographs look good. If you go, ask clearly about the actual route, walking time, difficulty and whether a guide is required.

sections.heading: “Going to a stream” does not mean the same thing at all three places
sections.body:
Suoi Da Ban is known for large rock slabs and picnic potential. Suoi Tien is more about forest, natural space and a slower outing. Da Ngon is more exploratory and asks more from your fitness and comfort on rough terrain.
Choose according to the group:
• Young children or older adults: favour easy access, short walking sections and places to rest.
• Friends wanting a picnic: Da Ban may work when weather is favourable.
• People who enjoy forest walks: consider Suoi Tien, with proper preparation.
• Experienced trekkers: only then consider harder routes such as Da Ngon.

sections.heading: The water season creates both the scenery and the risk
sections.body:
The wet season often brings fuller streams, clearer waterfall forms and more dramatic scenery. Suoi Da Ban is often described as attractive around May-November, but that is also when trails are wetter, rocks are more slippery and currents may be stronger.
Do not treat “more water” as automatically better. Before going, ask:
• Has there been heavy rain recently?
• Can the stream rise quickly?
• Is the access road muddy or slippery?
• Are any sections closed or unreachable?
• Are swimming areas safe for non-swimmers?
After heavy rain, avoid moving deep into the stream bed or standing beneath waterfalls. Do not camp immediately beside the water because the level can change quickly.

visitor_questions: Can an ordinary vehicle reach the access point today?
How long is the walk from the parking point to the stream?
Are the water level and slippery rocks suitable for young children or older adults?
Has there been heavy rain or any recent rising-water warning?
Which areas are open for swimming and which should be avoided?
Is a local guide or other support available for deeper sections of the route?

sources.label: VisitPhuQuoc - Suoi Da Ban
VisitPhuQuoc - Suoi Tien, Phu Quoc

activity_tour_3_islands.lede:
“Three-island tour” is the name of a common itinerary format in the An Thoi archipelago, not one fixed set of three islands used by every operator on every day. Popular routes often mention Hon Mong Tay, Hon Gam Ghi and Hon May Rut, but the order, stops and time spent at each can change.
It is a full-day sea excursion, usually combining speedboat or boat travel, swimming, snorkelling, lunch and time on an island. The quality therefore depends less on how many island names appear in the brochure and more on how the operator allocates time and responds when sea conditions change.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A full day at sea with several legs and several stops
infographic.note:
A typical three-island tour can include:
• Hotel pick-up and transfer to the port.
• Speedboat or boat travel into the An Thoi archipelago.
• One or more swimming stops.
• Snorkelling.
• Lunch and a rest period.
• Optional extras such as a coral park or seawalker experience.
• Return to the port and transfer back.
From pick-up to finish, the day can last around 8-10 hours, while the time actually spent in the water is usually much shorter than the total time spent travelling, organising equipment and eating.
A tour labelled “three islands” does not mean three separate full experiences. One island may be the snorkelling stop, another the lunch stop and another mainly for swimming or photographs.

infographic.label: QUALITY
infographic.value: Time in the water matters more than the number of stops
infographic.note:
A good itinerary should make clear:
• How long each stop lasts.
• How many minutes are genuinely available for swimming or snorkelling.
• Which stop is the main reef.
• Whether lunch is on an island or aboard the boat.
• Travel time between stops.
• How many guests are on the speedboat.
• Whether help is available for weak swimmers.
Fewer stops with enough water time can be better than racing through many islands for 20-30 minutes each. Travellers who care most about snorkelling should favour an itinerary with substantial reef time rather than one built mainly around photographs and meals.

infographic.label: BEFORE YOU GO
infographic.value: Check the sea and confirm the boat
infographic.note:
Good weather on land does not automatically mean the sea around An Thoi is suitable. Check wind, waves, rain, underwater visibility and the operator's route-change policy.
Also confirm:
• Whether the trip uses a boat or speedboat.
• Meeting point and pick-up time.
• The islands expected that day.
• Which activities are included.
• Which costs are extra.
• Whether life jackets, masks, snorkels and fins are provided.
• What happens if the sea is rough or an island cannot be reached.

sections.heading: Do not buy the tour from a list of island names alone
sections.body:
The An Thoi archipelago has many possible stops. A good operator should explain the real time at sea, time at each stop, included activities and the backup plan if conditions change.
An attractive island name does not guarantee a good experience. A reef may be quiet, clear and comfortable one day, then crowded, murky or rough on another.

sections.heading: Coral is not a tour prop
sections.body:
When snorkelling, do not stand on coral, break it, touch it or lift marine animals out of the water. Avoid feeding fish simply to gather them into a photograph.
Listen to instructions about entry points, boat traffic and keeping distance from the reef. A good visit leaves the ecosystem in the same condition after the group departs.

visitor_questions: Which islands are you planning to stop at today, and why?
How much actual snorkelling time is included?
Which stop is the main snorkelling site?
Where is lunch served, and can the menu change by day?
What is the alternative if sea conditions change?
How many guests and how many staff will be on the speedboat?

sources.label: VisitPhuQuoc - Snorkelling around Hon Thom, 21 August 2026
VisitPhuQuoc - Hon Roi, snorkelling and fishing

activity_snorkeling_an_thoi.lede:
Snorkelling lets you observe a reef from the surface using a mask and snorkel, with fins and a life jacket added depending on the tour. It is more accessible than scuba diving, but still requires suitable sea conditions, properly fitting equipment and guides who know how to organise people safely in the water.
It should not be described as “just put your face in the water”. Weak swimmers can panic if a mask leaks, the snorkel is used incorrectly, there is a current or they cannot see the bottom.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A limited water activity within a wider sea itinerary
infographic.note:
Snorkelling is usually organised at one or more reef sites and involves several steps:
• Travel from the pier or island to the snorkelling site.
• Safety briefing and equipment check.
• Entering the water as a group.
• Observing the reef for a set period.
• Returning to the boat or speedboat at the agreed time.
Time spent at the site is not the same as time spent snorkelling. Ask how many minutes are actually in the water, how large the group is and whether individual support is available.

infographic.label: EQUIPMENT
infographic.value: Mask, snorkel, fins and a life jacket depending on the tour
infographic.note:
A mask must fit the face properly to limit water leaking in. Guests should be shown how to position the snorkel and clear water from it. Fins make swimming easier but can also make a beginner feel less balanced until they get used to them.
A life jacket is not a sign that someone is a poor swimmer. It is an important safety aid, especially in current, crowded water or for anyone unfamiliar with open-sea swimming.

infographic.label: GOOD CONDITIONS
infographic.value: Clear enough water, manageable waves and a moderate current
infographic.note:
Underwater visibility changes with:
• Recent rain.
• Wind and waves.
• Current.
• Tide.
• The number of boats and visitors at the site.
• Light conditions during the day.
A reef that was crystal-clear before will not look the same every day. If the water is murky or waves are strong, the quality of the experience may drop even if the boat still reaches the planned location.

sections.heading: Easy to try does not mean safety can be ignored
sections.body:
People who are not strong swimmers can still snorkel in suitable conditions with a life jacket and proper support, but nobody should be pressured into the water if they are frightened or the sea is poor.
Beginners should practise breathing in shallow water or beside the boat before moving further away. Young children need direct adult supervision rather than being left entirely to a guide in a crowded sea area.

sections.heading: The quality of a snorkelling site changes from day to day
sections.body:
Water clarity, current and boat traffic directly affect the experience. Do not judge a site only from promotional photographs taken on an ideal day.
When the sea is unsuitable, shortening the session or moving to another site is better than forcing the original plan simply to complete the advertised list of activities.

visitor_questions: What are the water clarity and current like today?
How much actual time will we have in the water?
Are life jackets and individual support available for weak swimmers?
Do boats or speedboats pass close to this snorkelling area?
How is someone helped if they panic in the water?
Should I bring a prescription diving mask or any personal equipment?

activity_scuba.lede:
Scuba diving takes participants below the surface using a breathing cylinder and dedicated diving equipment. It is a technical activity that requires stronger safety procedures, professional supervision and more serious health screening than snorkelling.
For beginners, a try-dive can be organised with limited depth and duration under direct instructor supervision. It should not be described simply as “deeper snorkelling”.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A dive session includes briefing, equipment checks and time underwater
infographic.note:
A scuba programme usually has several stages:
• Travel to the dive site.
• Health declaration.
• Theory briefing and underwater hand signals.
• Equipment fitting, checks and practice.
• Diving with an instructor or dive professional.
• Surfacing, resting and monitoring how the diver feels.
• One or more dives depending on the programme.
The total time from departure to finish is much longer than the actual time underwater. Beginners should confirm whether they are buying a single introductory dive or a multi-dive programme, the planned depth and the instructor-to-guest ratio.

infographic.label: HOW IT DIFFERS FROM SNORKELLING
infographic.value: Breathing from a cylinder underwater and dealing with pressure changes
infographic.note:
Scuba allows a participant to remain underwater longer and go deeper than snorkelling, but requires learning how to:
• Breathe steadily through the regulator.
• Equalise ear pressure.
• Use hand signals.
• Control buoyancy and distance.
• Respond if there is a problem with the mask or regulator.
• Return to the surface under instruction.
A beginner should never descend deeper on their own or separate from the instructor. A non-certification experience should include direct supervision, controlled depth and proper equipment.

infographic.label: BEFORE DIVING
infographic.value: Declare health conditions and plan the time after the dive
infographic.note:
Ear or sinus problems, respiratory conditions, heart disease, blood-pressure issues, a history of fainting, recent surgery or some medications can affect diving suitability. Do not hide medical information simply because you are worried about missing the activity.
After diving, avoid scheduling a flight or another significant pressure-change activity too soon. The exact waiting period depends on the dive profile, number of dives, depth and the advice of the qualified operator.

sections.heading: This is a technical activity, not just a deeper version of reef viewing
sections.body:
The value of scuba is the experience of breathing underwater, observing marine life in three dimensions and learning how to move through the underwater environment.
Beginners should favour an operator that provides:
• A clear briefing.
• A health questionnaire.
• Properly fitting, checked equipment.
• An appropriate instructor-to-guest ratio.
• A procedure for panic or early termination.
• Transparent information about planned depth and duration.

sections.heading: Ask about safety standards before asking about photographs
sections.body:
Find out who will supervise the dive, what certification or training they hold, how many guests they supervise, how equipment is checked and what happens if a guest becomes uncomfortable underwater.
Do not choose a dive only because the photos look good or the price is lower. In an underwater activity, supervision quality matters more than the number of photo stops.

visitor_questions: What certification does the instructor hold, and how many guests do they supervise?
Is this an introductory dive for a beginner or a programme for certified divers?
Is there a health questionnaire before diving?
What depth and underwater time are planned?
How is the equipment checked and replaced when necessary?
How long should I wait after this dive before flying?

activity_seawalker.lede:
Seawalker lets visitors walk underwater while breathing through an air-supplied helmet instead of carrying a scuba cylinder. It is designed to be easier for first-timers, but it still requires instruction, controlled depth, suitable equipment and basic health screening.
Not needing to swim or scuba dive does not mean the activity suits everyone. Water pressure, the sensation of being below the surface and wearing an enclosed helmet can make some people anxious.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A controlled underwater walking route with limited time below the surface
infographic.note:
A typical experience includes:
• Travel to the seawalker area.
• A briefing and basic health check.
• Fitting the air-supplied helmet.
• Descending by steps or a guided platform.
• Walking along a set route and observing coral and fish.
• Returning to the surface and removing the equipment.
In some programmes, actual underwater time is only around 15-20 minutes, while preparation and waiting take longer.
Ask “how many minutes are actually underwater?” rather than relying only on the total advertised activity duration.

infographic.label: EQUIPMENT
infographic.value: Air-supplied helmet and a controlled walking route
infographic.note:
Participants breathe inside an air-supplied helmet often compared in appearance to an astronaut helmet. It removes the need to hold a snorkel in the mouth or carry a scuba cylinder, but guests still need to adjust to pressure and moving carefully underwater.
The route is normally controlled and supported by staff. Do not leave the marked path, touch marine life or use coral as a handhold to keep your balance.

infographic.label: WHAT TO ASK
infographic.value: Health, age limits and comfort with pressure
infographic.note:
Do not assume the activity is suitable for everyone simply because no diving experience is required. Ask about:
• Minimum age.
• Ear and sinus conditions.
• Respiratory conditions.
• Heart or blood-pressure problems.
• Actual underwater duration.
• What happens if a guest wants to surface early.
• Whether a guide stays with participants throughout the route.
Age limits can differ between operators, so confirm directly with the operator rather than relying on one general figure.

sections.heading: Designed to make underwater viewing accessible to beginners
sections.body:
Seawalker can suit people who want to see coral and fish at close range without learning scuba techniques. The slow walking format may also appeal to someone who does not want to swim continuously.
But this is not free-form diving. The route, time, depth and pace are controlled. Its value is accessibility, not adventure intensity.

sections.heading: Easy to join still does not mean health screening can be skipped
sections.body:
Ear or sinus problems, respiratory conditions, heart or blood-pressure issues and anxiety underwater should be discussed with the operator before descending.
A guest may not need to know how to swim, but they still need to remain calm, follow instructions and signal immediately if they have ear pain, difficulty breathing or feel unwell.

visitor_questions: Who should not take part in this activity?
Is ear-pressure equalisation explained before descending?
How much actual time is spent underwater?
Does a guide stay close throughout the route?
Can a guest surface early if they panic or develop ear pain?
Does the walking area protect coral and limit physical contact with it?

activity_big_game_fishing.lede:
Big-game fishing from An Thoi is a specialist, longer sea trip rather than a short fishing add-on. The experience depends on fishing grounds, equipment, the captain, technique and the ability to move when current, wind or fish signals change - not on a promise that a large fish is guaranteed.
This is fishing in the natural environment. Even a good crew, good boat and good equipment cannot make the catch a guaranteed outcome.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A long sea trip with many hours and several operational stages
infographic.note:
A big-game fishing trip typically includes:
• Transfer from the hotel to the pier.
• Preparing the boat, bait and equipment.
• Running out to the fishing grounds.
• Fishing one or more spots.
• Moving if current or fish activity is unfavourable.
• Rest, food and handling any catch where applicable.
• Return to port.
The trip can last many hours, sometimes close to a full day. Time with a rod in hand may not make up most of the journey because the boat needs to travel between fishing areas.
Distinguish a dedicated fishing trip from an island tour that includes 30-60 minutes of casual fishing. They are different products in boat setup, equipment, objective and expectation.

infographic.label: TECHNIQUE
infographic.value: Bottom fishing, jigging or another technique depending on the grounds
infographic.note:
The method depends on:
• Depth.
• Current.
• Target species.
• Season and weather.
• Type of bait or lure.
• The captain's and angler's ability.
A trip may use bottom fishing, jigging or another method depending on the location. Do not assume “big-game fishing” always means one fixed technique.
Equipment may include rods, reels, line, bait or lures, weights, hooks and fish-finding electronics. Ask clearly about the quantity, quality and condition of the gear before booking.

infographic.label: NO GUARANTEED CATCH
infographic.value: Catch quantity cannot be promised
infographic.note:
Wild fish depend on season, current, water temperature, bait, fishing grounds and many other variables beyond an operator's control. An operator can commit to the boat, equipment, duration and technical support - but should not promise that a large fish will definitely be caught.
If there is a policy on changing fishing grounds, rescheduling or service compensation when there is no catch, read the actual conditions rather than relying only on a verbal sales promise.

sections.heading: A dedicated fishing trip is different from a fishing stop on an island tour
sections.body:
A long fishing trip needs the right boat, equipment, a captain who understands the grounds and the freedom to move if conditions are poor. If fishing is the real purpose of the day, do not choose a tour simply because the word “fishing” appears in the itinerary.
Ask how much time will actually be spent fishing, whether each guest has their own equipment and how much hands-on support the crew provides. A professional trip is more than taking guests offshore and handing them a rod.

sections.heading: Sea conditions and stamina should be considered from the start
sections.body:
A multi-hour offshore trip can cause more seasickness and fatigue than a normal island excursion. Participants should:
• Check the wind and wave forecast.
• Eat a light meal before departure.
• Prepare suitable motion-sickness medication if needed.
• Bring a hat, sun protection and drinking water.
• Ask about rest areas and toilets aboard.
• Avoid heavy alcohol consumption before or during the trip.
For older guests or anyone prone to seasickness, consider the trip duration and boat type before booking.

visitor_questions: How many hours will we spend at sea?
What fishing gear and fish-finding equipment are used?
Does each guest have their own rod?
Can the captain move to another fishing ground based on current, wind and fish signals?
Does the price include bait, equipment, food and any surcharges?
What happens if there is no catch or sea conditions are unsuitable?
Does the boat have proper rest space, a toilet and enough life jackets?

activity_squid_fishing.lede:
Night squid fishing is an after-sunset sea experience: the boat leaves the pier, lights are switched on, artificial jigs are lowered and guests wait for squid to approach. The enjoyment is in sitting out on the night sea, learning the technique and sharing the atmosphere - not in a promise that everyone will catch a large quantity.
The activity depends directly on sea conditions, seasonal winds, tide and current, light, fishing area and crew experience. It is better understood as a chance to try a traditional night-sea activity and relax, not as a guaranteed catch.

infographic.label: SCALE
infographic.value: A sea trip lasting several hours with more than just fishing
infographic.note:
A night squid-fishing tour usually includes more than the time spent holding a rod. The itinerary may involve:
• Transfer from a hotel or meeting point to the pier.
• Boarding and settling into a place on the boat.
• Watching sunset or travelling to the fishing area.
• Learning how to use the rod and artificial jig.
• Fishing after dark.
• A snack, meal or preparation of the catch depending on the tour.
• Return to the pier and transfer back to accommodation.
Actual time at sea is often several hours, while the full door-to-door trip can be considerably longer. Anyone prone to seasickness should ask about time aboard, boat type and fishing area before booking.

infographic.label: HOW IT WORKS
infographic.value: Lights, artificial jigs and a controlled jigging motion
infographic.note:
Boats commonly use lights to create conditions that attract squid, then show guests how to lower an artificial jig, manage the line and move the rod appropriately.
Beginners should understand that squid fishing does not feel exactly like ordinary rod fishing. Recognising the weight of a squid and retrieving the line takes guidance from the crew. Do not change position, cast far from the boat or handle gear while the vessel is moving unless instructed.
Depending on the tour, each guest may receive a separate rod or equipment may be shared. The number of rods, condition of the jigs, standing space and crew support all affect the experience.

infographic.label: DON'T EXPECT
infographic.value: That going out guarantees a catch
infographic.note:
Wild squid depend on season, tide and current, weather, light and sea conditions. Some nights produce a good catch; others produce only a little or none at all.
If the tour cooks what guests catch, ask how it works: whether squid is prepared on board, whether the catch is shared among the group, whether there is any quantity limit and whether the meal is included in the ticket price.

sections.heading: A visitor experience rooted in the rhythm of fishing after dark
sections.body:
Night squid fishing gives travellers a small taste of life on the sea after sunset: lights reflecting on the water, waiting, working the line and accepting that nature decides what happens next.
Some tours are described as departing from Duong Dong or An Thoi, but the pier and fishing area can change with seasonal winds, sea conditions and each operator's organisation. A pier named in an old itinerary should not be treated as fixed for every day.

sections.heading: Choose the departure area according to season and sea conditions
sections.body:
Before going, reconfirm:
• Whether the boat leaves from Duong Dong, An Thoi or another pier.
• Travel time from the hotel to the pier.
• Whether the fishing area is sheltered, offshore or near the islands.
• Boat type, group size and seating area.
• Wind and wave forecast and the possibility of cancellation.
• Whether there is a toilet, enough life jackets and help for seasick guests.
Anyone prone to motion sickness should eat lightly before the trip, avoid alcohol and ask the operator which seating area has less movement. Young children should wear a correctly fitted life jacket and remain under direct adult supervision.

visitor_questions: Is today's boat departing from Duong Dong or An Thoi?
How long will we be at sea in total?
What is the boat's maximum passenger capacity?
Are tonight's sea conditions suitable for someone prone to seasickness?
Does each guest have a separate fishing rod or is equipment shared?
If no squid are caught, does the meal change?
Can the squid we catch be cooked on board?
Are the meal, drinking water and motion-sickness medication included in the price?
If the weather turns bad, can the tour be rescheduled or refunded?
